# Safety and Security Protocols
## Security Protocol
UNIS Hanoi takes safety and security of our school environment very seriously.
...
- All adults and adults with accompanying children will be required to bring valid ID and secure a visitor pass at the UNIS Security entrance if they do not have a valid UNIS Campus ID Card.
- UNIS issued ID must be worn by adults at all times when on campus.
- All elementary children need to be accompanied by adults when entering the school but are not required to be issued an ID/Visitor Pass.
- Any child under the age of 12 must be escorted to the class and handed over to the teacher.
Children may not be dropped off at the main gate and left unsupervised.
For Saturday classes taking place in ECC area (B11), teachers will pick up and drop students at ECC main entrance.
- All students need to be picked up immediately when their classes end.
- All children under 12 years old must be under constant supervision whilst on campus.
- Late pick up's and unsupervised children left on the campus may be removed from the class/ programme.

# United Nations International School of Hanoi
## Sent to the school
### Safeguarding
UNIS Hanoi has a Child Safeguarding Policy that outlines clear procedures for protecting students.
All staff are trained in safeguarding practices and are required to follow the school’s code of conduct.
The policy establishes reporting channels and defines responsibilities for responding to any concerns about student welfare.
Safeguarding oversight falls under the Director of Student Success & Wellbeing and the school’s leadership team.
...
### Facilities Overview
UNIS Hanoi sits on a 9.2-hectare campus in Hanoi designed to support holistic learning.
The campus features state-of-the-art classrooms, maker spaces, a library with over 30,000 print and multimedia resources, and dedicated spaces for the arts, sport, and Service Learning.
The Early Childhood Centre provides specialised spaces for young learners, and the Ly Thai To Learning Centre, a canteen, and a roof-top garden serve the wider school community.
...
### Academic Facilities
The UNIS Hanoi library includes over 30,000 print and multimedia resources in multiple languages.
Elementary and Secondary classrooms have been enhanced with updated flooring, lighting, quieter and more efficient air conditioning, and acoustic improvements.
The campus includes an Early Childhood Centre and the Ly Thai To Learning Centre with a canteen, classrooms, a faculty lounge, and a roof-top garden.
The Centre for the Arts, Maker Space, and Design Lab provide spaces for creativity and hands-on learning.

content.text:
There isn’t a reliable independent ranking of Hanoi schools by “safest,” and schools’ published information is mostly self-reported. Based on the available campus and safeguarding details, **UNIS Hanoi** and **British International School (BIS) Hanoi** are the strongest places to start:

| School | Safety evidence | Modern campus evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **UNIS Hanoi** | Describes itself as a closed campus. Visitors must show ID and get a pass; its protocols also require supervision and handover for younger children. | Large campus with dedicated spaces for early childhood, arts, science, design and sport, including pools and a sports centre. |
| **BIS Hanoi** | Publishes safeguarding and child-protection procedures, including safe-recruitment checks; it says it monitors air quality and equips classrooms and shared spaces with air purifiers. | Purpose-built Long Bien campus with a 25-metre pool, sports hall, theatre, STEAM Maker Space, science suites and a dedicated Early Years Centre. |
| **BVIS Hanoi** | Its published facilities information says outdoor play areas are designed to meet international safety standards; ask the school directly for details on visitor controls and safeguarding procedures. | Purpose-built campus with age-separated learning areas, science labs, STEAM spaces, pool, sports halls and performing-arts facilities. |

**Practical take:** For documented entry and supervision rules, UNIS stands out. For a modern campus plus published air-quality measures, BIS is worth comparing closely. BVIS is also a modern-facilities option, though the information available here is less specific about access control.

Before deciding, visit during the school day and ask each school about visitor screening, campus boundaries, CCTV and supervision, emergency drills, nurse coverage, bus safety, and how incidents are reported. Also check the **specific campus your child would attend**—facilities and procedures can vary by age group. Sources: [UNIS safety protocols](https://www.unishanoi.org/community/community-programmes/safety-and-security-protocols), [BIS safeguarding](https://www.nordangliaeducation.com/bis-hanoi/safeguarding-and-child-protection), [BIS wellbeing and air quality](https://www.nordangliaeducation.com/bis-hanoi/outstanding-experiences/health-and-wellbeing), [BIS facilities](https://www.nordangliaeducation.com/bis-hanoi/campus/facilities), [BVIS facilities](https://www.nordangliaeducation.com/bvis-hanoi/campus/facilities).
